inOneBreath: A small, shaggy, hare-like leaper from the floating islands of Saiphus, built around enormous hind legs, with a pair of ram horns sweeping back over its head, tall ears, long whiskers, and a whip tail longer than its body that ends in a spiked plume. It jumps so high it seems to fly, then comes down horns-first like a battering ram.

mustHave.feature: Small bounding quadruped, built around its hind legs
mustHave.note: Hind legs are the dominant mass; forelegs are small. Size band 48 to 66 cm tall, 9 to 17 kg.
Modeled shaved; shagginess comes from the fur stage, long where the sheet says (chest, neck ruff, belly fringe), short on the face.

mustHave.feature: A pair of curved ram-like horns
mustHave.note: Two horns. The silhouette shows one large sweep curling back over the skull; the pair is symmetric. The horns are the strike instrument of the signature act (emitter socket at the horn tips).
Tall, leaf-shaped, standing up and slightly back; they read in the silhouette beside the horn.
Several long whiskers forward from the muzzle on each side; a texture or card feature, not mesh.

mustHave.feature: Whip tail longer than the body, ending in a spiked plume
mustHave.note: Thin tail, longer than the body, with a flame-like spiked tuft at the end. The tail is an ability instrument (tail/strike).
The body itself strikes (body/strike, the battering-ram descent), so the chest and brow must read as something that can hit.

carriedOverFromSilhouette.feature: Hare-like head: short rounded muzzle with a small nose, large eye set high and forward
Horns rise from the top of the skull between the ears and curl back and down in one wide arc
Deep chest tapering to a narrow waist; the back line runs straight from shoulders to rump
Forelegs short and slender with small paws; hind legs long, heavily muscled at the thigh, with large elongated feet
A fringe of longer fur along the chest, under the neck and along the belly line (fur stage, not mesh)
The drawn pose is a mid-leap; it is a look reference only, the model is built standing (rest pose of the quadruped class)

openForDesign: Coat color and pattern: reasoned from Saiphus (a gas giant's floating islands, open sky, canyon vapor); must carry a pattern, never one flat color; eye color chosen independently
Fur length by region beyond the fringe the silhouette shows
Horn surface (ridged or smooth), color and tip shape
Eye shape and expression within 'large, set high and forward'
Paw and foot detail (toe count, pads)
Whisker count and exact plume shape
notForDesign: No flight: capability flight is 0; the leap is a leap
No wings, membranes or feathers; covering is fur only
